newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia, Panama reach airline accord.
newsitem.headline: Colombia, Panama reach airline accord.

text.p: Panama's aviation authorities have agreed to allow Colombian airlines to fly routes to the United States and Central America from Panamanian airports, Colombian civil aviation officials said Monday.
The agreement, reached late Saturday in Colombia's Caribbean city of Cartagena, takes effect immediately, Manuel Leal, chairman of the Colombian Air Transportation Association, said.

As a result of the accord, Panama's Copa Airlines will reduce its weekly flights between Colombia and Panama from 35 to 28, while four Colombian airlines -- Aerovias Nacionales de Colombia SA, or Avianca, Aerolineas Centrales de Colombia, or ACES, Intercontinental and SAM -- will have a total 56 flights to Panama, Leal said.
No Colombian airline has yet announced firm plans for new routes via Panama City, taking advantage of the deal.

Colombia had complained for months that passenger flight arrangements between the two nations favored Panama's Copa. It had threatened harsh restrictions on Copa flights if changes were not made, Leal said.
